claims.text: On September 22nd, UTMB and OpenEvidence announced a collaboration that gives UTMB clinicians cited medical evidence from within the electronic health record.
claims.quote:
September 22, 2026
The University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) and OpenEvidence today announced a collaboration that brings evidence-based artificial intelligence directly into clinicians’ everyday workflows, giving UTMB physicians and other clinical users secure access to cited medical evidence from within the electronic health record.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED_WITH_QUOTE_CORRECTION: the claim text is supported. The quote shown here restores the page's U+2019 apostrophe. The submitted quote had U+0027, which is a byte mismatch against both the live page and the saved snapshot (see rejected). The dateline matched exactly. The live dateline line reads 'September 22, 2026 • 9:10 a.m. by Stephen Hadley' and the body follows it directly. The newline marks a fragment boundary that leaves out ' • 9:10 a.m. by Stephen Hadley'.

claims.text: The integration went live at UTMB in March.
claims.quote: The integration, which went live at UTMB in March, was developed to give clinicians access to AI-enabled information resources within existing clinical workflows.

claims.text: UTMB clinicians reach the platform with their standard UTMB enterprise credentials.
claims.quote: Clinicians access the platform using their standard UTMB enterprise credentials.

claims.text: Clinicians ask clinical questions in plain language and receive answers that include citations to medical literature, clinical guidelines and other sources.
claims.quote: Once authenticated, clinicians can ask clinical questions in natural language and receive responses that include citations to medical literature, clinical guidelines, and other authoritative sources.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT as rendered text. 'authoritative' sits on its own line in the snapshot, probably separate markup, so the single spacing matches rendered whitespace)

claims.text: UTMB says more than half of its clinicians actively use OpenEvidence for clinical decision support.
claims.quote: Today, more than half of UTMB clinicians actively use OpenEvidence for clinical decision support.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT. The body gives no clinician count, percentage or method, only 'Adoption data indicate' with no figures)

claims.text: UTMB has hospitals on four campuses and more than 100 clinics across Southeast Texas.
claims.quote: With hospitals located on four campuses in addition to more than 100 clinics across Southeast Texas
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT. '100' is the only numeral in the body. 'four' is spelled out. The sentence goes on with ', the geographic reach of UTMB makes rapid access to current medical knowledge particularly valuable.')

claims.text: UTMB reports growth in both the number of clinicians using OpenEvidence and the volume of queries since the March launch.
claims.quote: Since the March launch, UTMB has seen strong growth in both the number of clinicians using OpenEvidence and the volume of clinical queries submitted through the platform.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT in the body. The photo alt text has a different ending, 'clinical queries they submit', but the quote correctly follows the body)

claims.text: UTMB says it will keep evaluating use and clinician experience, and its release publishes no measure of whether the answers are accurate or whether patient care changed.
claims.quote: As adoption grows, UTMB will continue evaluating utilization, clinician experience, and opportunities to improve how evidence and clinical intelligence are delivered at the point of care.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT. 'accuracy', 'accurate', 'outcome', 'safety' and 'validation' are not in the body, and 'patient' appears only in site navigation. The body does say 'validated AI capabilities' and 'evaluated based on their real-world use and impact', but these describe a planned environment and give no measure)

claims.text: Under Texas Health and Safety Code Section 183.005, a health care practitioner may use artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes if conditions are met, including review of all records it creates.
claims.quote:
A health care practitioner may use artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes, including the use of artificial intelligence for recommendations on a diagnosis or course of treatment based on a patient's medical record, if:
the practitioner reviews all records created with artificial intelligence
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (both fragments FOUND-EXACT. The second fragment is 183.005(a)(3), and the newline leaves out (a)(1), (a)(2) and the '(3)' marker. The text says 'including', so it doesn't claim to list every condition. (a)(3) goes on with 'in a manner that is consistent with medical records standards developed by the Texas Medical Board.' SECTION 1 adds Chapter 183 to the Health and Safety Code. The apostrophe is straight on the source)

claims.text: The same section requires a practitioner who uses artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes to disclose that use to patients.
claims.quote: A health care practitioner who uses artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes as described by Subsection (a) must disclose the practitioner's use of that technology to the practitioner's patients.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT in 183.005(b). The apostrophes are straight on the source. 'clinical decision support' does not appear anywhere in the bill)

claims.text: Under a Texas law in effect since January 1st, 2026, a provider that uses an artificial intelligence system in a health care service must disclose it to the patient by the date the service is first provided, except in an emergency.
claims.quote: If an artificial intelligence system is used in relation to health care service or treatment, the provider of the service or treatment shall provide the disclosure under Subsection (b) to the recipient of the service or treatment or the recipient's personal representative not later than the date the service or treatment is first provided, except in the case of emergency
claims.source_type: primary_official (enrolled H.B. 149, Business and Commerce Code Sec. 552.051(f))
claims.verdict: VERIFIED_WITH_NOTE (FOUND-EXACT in 552.051(f). The bill's SECTION 10 reads 'This Act takes effect January 1, 2026.' and SECTION 4 places it in the Business & Commerce Code. The quote stops before ', in which case the provider shall provide the required disclosure as soon as reasonably possible.' The claim text is accurate as a deadline rule, but it could be read as saying emergencies need no disclosure at all. If this claim is ever used on screen or in narration, state the as-soon-as-reasonably-possible duty. 552.051 does not define 'provider')

claims.text: The UT System's REAL Health AI page names Qualified Health as its partner and does not mention Abridge or OpenEvidence.
claims.quote: Partnering with Qualified Health to enable secure, AI-driven clinical communications across all UT institutions.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED (FOUND-EXACT under 'Secure Chat Deployment -'. 'Abridge' and 'OpenEvidence' are not on the page. There is no publication or last-updated date, only a footer '© 2026')

rejected.claim: c1 quote field as submitted in out/dispatch/claims.json: 'clinicians' everyday workflows' with a straight apostrophe (U+0027)
rejected.reason: Not verbatim byte for byte. The live UTMB page has 'clinicians’ everyday workflows' with U+2019. I confirmed this in 2 separate fetches, and the director's own snapshot out/dispatch/sources/utmb.validator.txt line 43 has U+2019 too. The words are identical and the claim text is fully supported, so the claim stays verified. Only the submitted quote string fails. Fix: restore U+2019 in the quote field, or write down that the fragment check normalizes apostrophes. Its current note, 'confirmed verbatim in the saved snapshot', is not literally true at byte level. The narration does not quote this sentence, so the film is not affected.

validation.source: Independent validator leaf (claude-opus-5-5, high effort, isolated context, no sub-agents). I re-fetched every URL with WebFetch on 2026-10-11. The tool refuses to return full verbatim page text, so I checked each quote with per-string exact-match queries (FOUND-EXACT, FOUND-WITH-DIFFERENCES or NOT FOUND, with differences given character by character). I asked separately about apostrophe code points, subsection lettering, effective dates and code names. I also compared the UTMB result against the director's snapshot out/dispatch/sources/utmb.validator.txt, which I read in full. I did not take any researcher or director summary as evidence.
rejected: c1: the submitted quote string has U+0027 where the live page and saved snapshot have U+2019 ('clinicians’'). The claim is verified, but the quote field needs a byte correction or a written normalization rule. I count this as a recordkeeping defect, not a factual one.

c11: the quote stops before ', in which case the provider shall provide the required disclosure as soon as reasonably possible.' The claim text is accurate but incomplete about emergencies. It is not used in the current narration. Add the clause before any on-screen or spoken use.

c9: the quote joins 183.005(a)'s opening with (a)(3), leaving out (a)(1) and (a)(2) without an ellipsis. The newline follows the file's fragment convention and the text says 'including', so this is not misleading. Recorded for transparency only.

I agree with the 6 rejections already in claims.json. The researcher's S.B. 1188 quote with an ellipsis really did drop the conditions. The double-spaced 'other  authoritative  sources' does not match the rendered text. The Abridge vendor page lists 'UT Medical Branch' in an institution list and names Peter McCaffrey as a UT Medical Branch officer, but it never says UTMB uses Abridge. 'Galveston' appears on the UTMB page only in the footer '© The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston'. No fetched source supports the Board of Regents testimony sentence. 'Without leaving' is not the source's wording.

No other defect found. Scope checked: c1 to c12 in claims.json, all 10 research.json findings and their quotes (including the Abridge quote, FOUND-EXACT, release dated October 8, 2026), the 3 sources in story_selection.json, and all 8 lines of vo_script.txt.
required_edits_applied: Line 1, 'A UTMB clinician asks a question. The answer comes back with its sources.' Supported by c4. Applied.

Line 2, 'announced ... on September twenty-second, and says it went live in March.' The date traces to c1's quoted dateline 'September 22, 2026', which the director added so the spoken date is backed by a quote. That edit is applied and confirmed on the live page. 'went live in March' is c2. One note: the line says UTMB 'announced the OpenEvidence AI tool' where c1 says 'announced a collaboration'. That is a compression, not a factual error.
Line 3, 'sign in with their usual credentials, and ask in plain language.' Supported by c3 (standard UTMB enterprise credentials) and c4 (natural language). Applied.
Line 4, 'The answers carry citations. To medical literature and clinical guidelines.' A subset of c4. It drops 'other authoritative sources' but adds nothing unsupported. Applied.

Line 5, 'UTMB says more than half of its clinicians now use it for clinical decision support.' This is c5, attributed to UTMB. 'more than half' is the release's own wording, so no figure was derived and there is no numeral. Applied.

Line 6, 'That is UTMB's own report. The release publishes no measure of accuracy or patient care.' This is c5's self-report scope plus c8. I confirmed on the live page that the body gives no accuracy, error-rate, outcome or patient-care measure. Applied.

Line 7, 'A citation shows where an answer says it came from. It doesn't show the answer is right.' This is editorial reasoning that matches c4's scope note, not a sourced fact. It contradicts no source and claims nothing about any particular answer. Acceptable as framing.
Line 8, 'UTMB says it will keep evaluating use and clinician experience.' Supported by c8. Applied.

Conditional and legal wording: the narration makes no legal claim. It does not say S.B. 1188 or H.B. 149 (c9 to c11) applies to UTMB, that a decision-support question counts as diagnostic use, or anything about telling patients. It does not mention Abridge, and it does not place the story in Galveston County. The unsupported Board of Regents sentence is not in the narration. Every required scope limit holds.
Numerals: the narration has none. The date is spoken as words and backed by the numeral in c1's quote, so the rubric's numeral-in-quote hard fail is not triggered.
House rules in the narration: no colons, semicolons, em or en dashes, first person, sentences opening with 'And' or 'But', 'cannot', or the banned words gap, matters or pattern.
Not yet applied: the c1 quote apostrophe byte correction in claims.json. The narration is not affected.
Not yet applied, advisory: c11's text should state the emergency 'as soon as reasonably possible' duty before any use. It is not in the current narration.

Board wording note: story_selection.json agency.who_can_act still says 'The UT System Board of Regents meets in public and takes testimony on agenda topics.' No fetched source supports it and claims.json rejected it, so it must not reach board copy. The county and viewer_question 'Galveston' are the Docket's editorial placement, not something the release says.
